text: The data platform ingests events from checkout, search, and support systems. Events are validated, deduplicated, encrypted, and written to object storage. A daily job produces customer metrics. A change request must include a rollback owner and an approval timestamp. Raw checkout events contain order identifiers, currency, tax, discount, and fulfillment state. Search events contain query language, result count, and click position. Support events contain case priority, assignment time, and resolution category. The platform writes immutable source partitions before deriving any aggregate. Data quality checks compare source count, destination count, duplicate rate, and null rate. An alert is opened when counts diverge for two consecutive intervals. The on-call engineer records the affected partition and customer impact in the incident channel. A backfill first runs in an isolated staging account. The backfill owner confirms encryption keys and storage policy before copy. The metrics job publishes a daily freshness timestamp. Finance receives monthly reconciled revenue totals. Product receives weekly funnel totals. Security reviews access logs every seven days. Operations documents every recovery exercise. A migration never drops a source field until downstream consumers confirm their cutover. Each production change has a unique change identifier and a peer reviewer. The deployment coordinator records the approval timestamp in UTC. The service objective is measured monthly and the report includes all missed windows.
